## Overview This PR is to revert the changes in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58173, and to add a check to make sure this doesn't happen again. I believe what happened was that a local old version of QuTLASS, before it was migrated to the stable ABI, was being built against the new flags that help ensure QuTLASS stays stable. So I also added a check in here to make sure that a version of QuTLASS after this update is being used. This checks for the file `qutlass/csrc/include/registration.h` which was only added after the migration. cc @Harry-Chen @janeyx99 ## Validation **main branch:** [torch-abi-audit](https://pypi.org/project/torch-abi-audit/) vllm: **this branch** build succeeds and `[STABLE ] [abi3-ok ] _qutlass_C.abi3.so (stable_shim=60, unstable=0) min-torch=2.11.0` Note: the drop in the number of stable_shim comes from internal implementation differences in torch/stable. Particularly the inclusions of `torch_exception_get_what`, `torch_exception_get_what_without_backtrace`, and `torch_new_stable_ivalue` in 2.13. ---
Pull Request Checklist - [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity. - [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI. - [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples. - [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.

/ci run
✅ Triggered [Buildkite CI #95380](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/95380) for commit `4e19ec8050f3`.

@yewentao256, as @ZJY0516 and @Harry-Chen mentioned, this can allow users to use their own pytorch version and help enforce ABI stability.

For some additional context, with the current setup, QuTLASS could use symbols that are allowed under whatever version it's built with (in this case 2.13). So vLLM now has a minimum torch version of 2.13, when it could have as low as 2.11 (see new image of torch-abi-audit in description). Migrating vLLM to the stable ABI allows us to build against one PyTorch version and run against any version at or above TORCH_TARGET_VERSION, without rebuilding. However, because of this single dependency, we're unnecessarily excluding two PyTorch versions that vLLM could otherwise support. This could be inconvenient for developers who want to use older PyTorch versions without rebuilding, as well as distributors who want to package wheels for multiple PyTorch versions without maintaining a separate build for each one.

And as @Harry-Chen mentioned, this flag help us enforce that QuTLASS does not bring in any unstable symbols (the bug that caused the original PR was really a feature!). There is a CI check as well to make sure this doesn't happen, but this is an extra safeguard in case that CI check fails.    

I am not surprised that this has not caused bugs, as it's a very particular use case, and a developer probably would've just updated python if they ran into this, but I still think it's worth adding it back for the reasons described above. 

Let me know what you think or if you have any questions!

1. backward compatibility
Yeah agree with @Harry-Chen, as we already list `torch==2.14.0` in requirements.txt so it is not the main concern

2. I am not actually against pinning a version, I am concerned as we already running torch 2.13 abi well for over 3+weeks, changing back to 2.11 is actually a breaking change.

So I am thinking we should pin 2.13 version instead?

> 2. I am not actually against pinning a version, I am concerned as we already running torch 2.13 abi well for over 3+weeks, changing back to 2.11 is actually a breaking change.

This should not be an issue IMHO. Anyhow we have not announced any ABI stability for vLLM yet. And setting the lowest possible torch version does not bring obvious harm.

I agree with @Harry-Chen that I doubt lowering it would bring harm. But, @yewentao256, if your concern is that Qutlass has been using 2.13 for weeks, and dropping it lower might break what we know works, then we could raise it to 2.13. I think it's better to have some torch_version instead of nothing.
It theoretically shouldn't make trouble if pinning 2.11, but still not well tested in current main branch. So agree with @cleonard530 pinning 2.13 would be better in current situation

For all libraries that depend on QuTLASS it would be ideal for the torch version pin to be as low as possible, but I understand the concern of not wanting to promise something that’s not well tested. Another thing to keep in mind is that this pin is mostly used as binary metadata and the README/documentation/runtime requirements can still recommend 2.13 as the tested version. This way we don’t block others from going off the beaten path and using the binary with 2.11 or 2.12.

Otherwise, is there a process for how we can test to ensure that 2.11 works well too?

@@ -51,6 +51,13 @@ endif()
 if(NOT qutlass_SOURCE_DIR)
   message(FATAL_ERROR "[QUTLASS] source directory could not be resolved.")
 endif()
+
+if(NOT EXISTS "${qutlass_SOURCE_DIR}/qutlass/csrc/include/registration.h")
+  message(FATAL_ERROR
+    "[QUTLASS] Stable ABI support was not found in the Qutlass source. "
+    "Please update your Qutlass package.")
+endif()
+
 message(STATUS "[QUTLASS] QuTLASS is available at ${qutlass_SOURCE_DIR}")
 
 if(${CMAKE_CUDA_COMPILER_VERSION} VERSION_GREATER_EQUAL 13.0)
@@ -142,9 +149,9 @@ if(${CMAKE_CUDA_COMPILER_VERSION} VERSION_GREATER_EQUAL 12.8 AND QUTLASS_ARCHS)
 
   target_compile_definitions(_qutlass_C PRIVATE
     QUTLASS_MINIMAL_BUILD=1
-    QUTLASS_DISABLE_PYBIND=1
     TARGET_CUDA_ARCH=${QUTLASS_TARGET_CC}
     CUTLASS_ENABLE_DIRECT_CUDA_DRIVER_CALL=1
+    TORCH_TARGET_VERSION=0x020B000000000000ULL
     USE_CUDA)
 
   set_property(SOURCE ${QUTLASS_SOURCES} APPEND PROPERTY COMPILE_OPTIONS

This way we don’t block others from going off the beaten path and using the binary with 2.11 or 2.12.

Otherwise, is there a process for how we can test to ensure that 2.11 works well too?
